findings.title: Denial cache key shares namespace with permission cache
findings.body: In pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go userPermDenialCacheKey builds namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent while userPermCacheKey builds namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action. A denial key can equal a permission key (e.g. perm action "a_b_c" vs denial action "a" name "b" parent "c"). They share the same underlying cache.Cache instance, so a permCache.Get can read a bool denial value and a permDenialCache.Get can read a map value. Both fail JSON unmarshal and log warnings, turning hits into misses and causing extra DB load. Use a distinct prefix such as ".perm_deny_".

findings.title: Denial cache key omits identity type causing cross-principal false deny
findings.body: In pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go Check builds permDenialKey from namespace, UserUID, action, name and parent only, before branching on IdentityType. Different identity types can share the same UserUID string (e.g. subject "anonymous:0" and "render:0" both yield UID "0", and "user:X" vs "service-account:X" can collide). A denial cached for one type will be returned for the other without ever consulting permissions, so renderer which should be allowed via wildcard for dashboards:read/folders:read can be incorrectly denied because anonymous was denied for the same resource, and vice versa.

findings.title: Denial cache short-circuits DB fallback and reintroduces stale deny
findings.body: In pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go Check returns Allowed:false immediately on permDenialCache hit without re-querying the DB. The rest of the PR adds fallback to the DB when cached permissions do not contain the resource precisely to see newly granted/created permissions. Once a resource is denied, the denial entry (30s TTL) blocks that fallback for its whole lifetime, so a grant made after the denial (including the creator-access case the PR fixes if the first check races creation) remains invisible until expiry. List in the same file does not even have the fallback and serves stale cached permission sets.
